script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Psychological
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

A dark and quiet living room. MARGARET, mid 40s, sits on a worn-out couch, staring at the TV. She chews on her lower lip, her eyes red from crying. She turns off the TV.

MARGARET
(whispers to herself)
I can't do this anymore.

Suddenly, the front door creaks open. The silhouette of a man appears in the doorway. MARGARET's heart races. She stands up, ready to face him.

INT. HALLWAY - NIGHT

JAMES, late 40s, steps into the house, wearing a trench coat and carrying a bouquet of roses.

JAMES
Margaret, I'm home.

MARGARET
(pauses, then speaks)
Why are you here?

JAMES
I came to talk.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

They sit across from each other. The tension between them is palpable.

MARGARET
(angry)
I don't want to hear it, James. I can't forgive you for what you've done.

JAMES
(sad)
I know. And I understand why you can't. But I want to try to make things right. I want to start over.

MARGARET
(disgusted)
Start over? After everything you've taken from me?

JAMES
(tearfully)
I know I've made mistakes. I've hurt you, and for that, I'm truly sorry. But I can't change the past. I can only promise to do better in the future.

MARGARET
(sighs)
James, I don't know if I can forgive you. I don't know if I even want to.

INT. KITCHEN - DAY

MARGARET stands at the counter, making breakfast. JAMES enters the kitchen, wearing an apron and holding a plate.

JAMES
(smiling)
I made pancakes. Your favorite.

MARGARET
(surprised)
You did?

JAMES
(nods)
Yes. I thought we could start our day fresh.

MARGARET
(hesitates, then sits at the table)
Fine. We'll try.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

They sit on the couch, watching a movie. MARGARET leans her head on JAMES' shoulder. He puts his arm around her.

MARGARET
(softly)
I'm trying to forgive you, James. But it's not easy.

JAMES
(whispers in her ear)
I know. And I'll be patient. I'll be here for you, every step of the way.

They sit in silence, watching the movie. The tension between them begins to dissipate.

INT. MARGARET'S STUDIO - DAY

MARGARET sits at her painting easel, lost in thought. JAMES enters the studio, carrying a sketchpad and pencils.

JAMES
(quietly)
May I join you?

MARGARET
(looks up, surprised)
Of course.

They work together in silence, each lost in their own thoughts.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

MARGARET sits on the couch, looking at a family photo album. JAMES sits next to her, holding her hand.

MARGARET
(tearfully)
I remember when we were happy. Before everything went wrong.

JAMES
(hugging her)
We can be happy again, Margaret. We just need to work through this.

MARGARET
(sighs)
I want to believe you, James. I really do.

INT. MARGARET'S BEDROOM - NIGHT

They lie in bed, facing each other.

MARGARET
(softly)
James, I forgive you.

JAMES
(relieved)
Thank you, Margaret. I won't let you down again.

They hold each other close, their bodies intertwined.

FADE OUT.

END OF SCREENPLAY.
